title: Mangroves and coastal ecosystems — issues brief
claim: Mangrove forests provide nursery habitat for fish and crustaceans and buffer coastlines from erosion, but are under sustained pressure from aquaculture expansion and land conversion, making native replanting a priority restoration action.
evidence_text: IUCN identifies conversion of mangrove forest to aquaculture ponds as one of the leading drivers of mangrove loss globally, removing nursery habitat that supports coastal fisheries and reducing natural buffering against storms and erosion. Restoration approaches favoured by IUCN prioritise replanting native mangrove species matched to local tidal and salinity conditions, focusing first on the most fragmented remaining patches to reconnect nursery habitat corridors.
